title: Lesson 38 impersonal and compound patientive NNC review

groups.title: Impersonal-patientive foundation
groups.proposal: Derive an impersonal patientive from the exact nonactive core of an owner-issued impersonal VNC Result. Preserve its complete Source, voice history, participants, and patientive result meaning, and keep it distinct from an agentive doer even where English translation is vague.
groups.readingJob: Show the active Source, impersonal operation, nonactive core, patientive Result, participant facts, and result-versus-doer contrast.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses the patientive formation only when another licensed deverbal analysis is genuinely available; the application captures the impersonal core and derives its consequences automatically.
groups.controlPolicy: Do not accept a raw nonactive-looking stem, copied Result, example identity, English participle label, formula, or surface as authority.

groups.title: lō intransitive impersonal-patientives
groups.proposal: From an exact impersonal VNC Result with a typed final lō boundary, delete final ō and retain l. Preserve repeated impersonal layers, root-plus-ya analysis, vowel quantity, noun class, and compositional or licensed lexical readings without using the examples as an admission list.
groups.readingJob: Show the owner-issued impersonal Result, typed lō boundary, retained l, repeated impersonal layers, root-plus-ya status, vowel behavior, class, and reading status.
groups.decisionSplit: The exact owner-issued VNC Result has already chosen any licensed root-plus-ya realization; Lesson 38 inherits it automatically and exposes only a genuinely unresolved lexical reading.
groups.controlPolicy: Do not infer root-plus-ya from letters alone, create an example-stem whitelist, or expose lō truncation, vowel quantity, class, or inherited impersonal layers as choices.

groups.title: ō and o-hua intransitive impersonal-patientives
groups.proposal: Derive the ō and o-hua impersonal patientive families from exact typed impersonal Results by removing the complete licensed nonactive material while preserving Source-shape history, repeated impersonal layers, noun class, and any typed irregular realization or lexical reading.
groups.readingJob: Show the exact impersonal Result, ō or o-hua boundary, removed material, retained Source, repeated impersonal structure, typed sound change, class, and meaning.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses only a genuinely available lexical or irregular analysis; the application derives regular boundary removal and inherited grammatical facts.
groups.controlPolicy: Do not turn witnessed e-to-a, ti-to-ch, or ci-to-x outcomes into general spelling rules or exact-stem route gates; preserve them as typed analysis where required.

groups.title: hua intransitive impersonal-patientives
groups.proposal: Delete typed nonactive hua from an exact impersonal Result, shorten preceding ī where licensed, preserve other vowel quantity and the full active-to-impersonal history, and keep alternative formations and lexical readings typed.
groups.readingJob: Show the typed hua boundary, removed suffix, preceding vowel, active Source, impersonal Result, alternative formation, class, and reading.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses only a genuinely licensed alternative formation or lexical reading; regular hua deletion and vowel behavior are automatic.
groups.controlPolicy: Do not expose vowel shortening, noun class, or example identity as user authority.

groups.title: hua-lō layered impersonal-patientives
groups.proposal: Preserve the layered hua plus lō Source and remove only the outer licensed nonactive material when deriving the impersonal patientive, retaining the inner hua history and typed patientive reading.
groups.readingJob: Show the inner hua formation, outer lō impersonal layer, removed material, retained stem, noun class, referent, and meaning.
groups.decisionSplit: The application derives the layered boundary behavior; the user chooses only a genuinely open lexical reading.
groups.controlPolicy: Do not flatten hua-lō into final letters or let the user manually choose which layer to delete.

groups.title: Reflexive and reciprocal impersonal-patientives
groups.proposal: Carry the shuntline ne and any remaining projective object from an exact reflexive or reciprocal impersonal VNC Result into the patientive Source, keeping the impersonal and passive analyses distinct even when their surfaces overlap.
groups.readingJob: Show active reflexive or reciprocal ancestry, impersonal transformation, shuntline ne, retained projective object, patientive Result, and overlap warning.
groups.decisionSplit: The application inherits ne and projective objects automatically; the user chooses an analysis only where exact Source evidence leaves genuine ambiguity.
groups.controlPolicy: Do not manually insert ne, reconstruct reflexivity from the nounstem surface, or merge passive and impersonal Sources.

groups.title: Projective-object foundation and lō patientives
groups.proposal: Preserve the nonhuman direct object as mainline tla or shuntline tla inside an exact impersonal patientive Result, including double-object tē+tla structure, lō truncation, and only typed root-plus-ya variants.
groups.readingJob: Show active objects, impersonal Source, mainline or shuntline tla, lō boundary, root-plus-ya variant, noun class, referent, and meaning.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses only a genuinely licensed root-plus-ya or lexical variant; object placement and lō truncation follow typed participant structure automatically.
groups.controlPolicy: Do not infer human or nonhuman reference from prefix order, delete objects arbitrarily, or whitelist example stems.

groups.title: Projective-object ō patientives
groups.proposal: Derive projective-object impersonal patientives from exact ō Sources while preserving tla or tē+tla structure, typed Source-shape realizations, noun class, compositional meaning, and licensed lexical specialization.
groups.readingJob: Show object structure, ō boundary, Source shape, derived realization, class, compositional meaning, and lexical specialization.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses only a genuinely open lexical reading; participant and boundary consequences are automatic.
groups.controlPolicy: Do not use example identity or English meaning to authorize the route or object pattern.

groups.title: Projective-object hua patientives
groups.proposal: Delete typed hua from exact projective-object impersonal Results, retain tla placement, and derive preceding-vowel and final-a behavior from complete Source structure while preserving homophony and lexical readings.
groups.readingJob: Show projective object, hua boundary, active final vowel, derived vowel, Source history, homophonous alternatives, class, referent, and meaning.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses only a genuine source-analysis or lexical ambiguity; productive hua and vowel behavior are automatic.
groups.controlPolicy: Do not decide homophony from the surface or create example-specific vowel rules.

groups.title: Human tē Source to tla impersonal patientive
groups.proposal: For a single-object human tē Source, preserve the passive-then-impersonal derivation that replaces tē with impersonal tla before lō patientive formation. Keep human referent, complete participant history, homonymous nonhuman Sources, number restrictions, and lexical readings distinct.
groups.readingJob: Show active human object, passive promotion, impersonal tla, lō truncation, human referent, homonym, number restriction, and meaning.
groups.decisionSplit: The application derives tē-to-tla from typed participant and voice history; the user chooses only a genuine homonymous Source or lexical reading.
groups.controlPolicy: Do not expose tē-to-tla as a free prefix replacement or infer humanness from the final nounstem.

groups.title: Human-source ō impersonal patientives
groups.proposal: Apply the same typed human tē to passive to impersonal tla pathway to ō Sources, removing ō and preserving the human patient, number behavior, possessive relations, and contrast with the corresponding passive patientive.
groups.readingJob: Show the human object Source, passive and impersonal stages, tla, removed ō, NNC paradigm facts, and passive-patientive contrast.
groups.decisionSplit: The application derives the full pathway; the user chooses only a genuinely open lexical reading.
groups.controlPolicy: Do not allow manual prefix replacement, participant relabeling, or surface-based source recovery.

groups.title: Human-source hua patientives and rare tē exceptions
groups.proposal: Derive ordinary human-source hua patientives through passive and impersonal tla, while preserving the rare human tē formations as explicitly typed lexical exceptions rather than productive alternatives.
groups.readingJob: Show active human object, passive and impersonal stages, tla or exceptional tē, hua deletion, vowel behavior, homonym, referent, and exception status.
groups.decisionSplit: The user may choose exceptional tē only when the typed lexical analysis licenses it; ordinary structural consequences are automatic.
groups.controlPolicy: Do not generalize the rare tē witnesses or make an exception picker authorize unrelated Sources.

groups.title: Human and nonhuman patientive contrasts
groups.proposal: Preserve contrasting tla human and tē nonhuman patientive readings through complete typed valence, voice, participant, and lexical histories. Treat anomalous tē formations as lexical analysis and keep single-object impersonal and double-object passive Sources distinct.
groups.readingJob: Show tla or tē, human or nonhuman referent, active valence, object roles, voice pathway, lexical anomaly, and competing Source analysis.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses only a genuine human/nonhuman or Source ambiguity left unresolved by typed facts; the application derives all fixed contrasts.
groups.controlPolicy: Do not infer referent class from prefix alone or turn anomalous examples into productive permission.

groups.title: Patientive and active-action translation overlap
groups.proposal: Keep impersonal patientive and active-action nounstems grammatically distinct when they share an English translation, using exact Source voice, derivational suffix, participant structure, and Result identity rather than meaning labels.
groups.readingJob: Show both exact Sources, their voice and derivational histories, their distinct Results, and the shared translation warning.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses an analysis only where context and typed Source do not already resolve it.
groups.controlPolicy: Do not merge analyses or authorize either route from English translation.

groups.title: Patientives from compound verb Sources
groups.proposal: Derive passive and impersonal patientives from complete typed compound VNC Results while preserving adverbial or object embeds, matrix, participant roles, internal boundaries, patient referent, and compositional or lexical reading.
groups.readingJob: Show compound embed, relation, matrix, participants, voice pathway, patientive boundary, referent, Nahuatl constituent order, English translation reversal, and lexical reading.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses the intended licensed compound relation or genuinely ambiguous reading; the application preserves the compound Result and derives patientive structure.
groups.controlPolicy: Do not flatten the compound into a string, guess the embed from translation, or whitelist witnessed compounds.

groups.title: Patientive Result as compound matrix
groups.proposal: Allow an exact owner-issued patientive NNC Result to serve as the matrix of a licensed compound nounstem, preserving its VNC ancestry, patientive derivation, matrix identity, embed relation, boundaries, and compositional or lexical meaning.
groups.readingJob: Show the captured patientive Result, its verbal ancestry, the nominal embed, embed-matrix relation, compound boundaries, resulting NNC, and meaning.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses the licensed embed and semantic relation; the application preserves the exact patientive matrix and derives boundary behavior.
groups.controlPolicy: Do not continue from a nounstem string, copied Result, formula, surface, or example identity.
